[[File:Kemah_09_1984_Karasutal.jpg|thumb|The [[Vixon]] river flowing through the region of modern Praesyu in Western Alzuria.]]
[[Alzuria (region)]] encompasses the land between the [[Tusil River|Tusil]] and [[Vixon River]] rivers. The Tusil gain their headwaters in the neighbouring [[Valmiran Mountains]] and further north in the [[Untschalle]], while the Vixon gains its waters from the [[Samarran Mountains]] to the west. Both rivers are fed by numerous tributaries, and the entire river system drains the vast mountainous region. The region has a mostly Mediterranean climate, with a vast desert expanse in the north. In the extreme south, the Tusil and the Vixon unite and empty into the [[Kadhif Gulf]].<ref>Broadbent, G., "The Ecology of the Kadhif", a, ''Eco-architecture II: Harmonization Between Architecture and Nature,'' WIT Press, 1723, pp. 15–26.</ref>

The [[Wikipedia:Aridity|arid]] environment ranges from the northern areas of rain-fed agriculture to the south, where irrigation of agriculture is essential. This irrigation is aided by a high water table and by melting snows from the high peaks of the western [[Valmiran Mountains]] and from the Samarran Mountains, the sources of the [[Tusil River|Tusil]] and [[Vixon River|Vixon Rivers]] that give the region its name. The usefulness of irrigation depends upon the ability to mobilise sufficient labour for the construction and maintenance of canals, and this, from the earliest period, has assisted the development of urban settlements and centralised systems of political authority.

Agriculture throughout the region has been supplemented by nomadic pastoralism, in which tent-dwelling nomads herded animals from the river pastures during the dry summer months and out onto seasonal grazing lands on the desert fringe during the wet winter season. The central Alzurian area is generally lacking in building stone, precious metals, and timber, and so has historically relied on long-distance trade in agricultural products to secure these items from outlying areas and the more mountainous regions of the west and east, which typically ruled the flat central portion. In the marshlands to the south of the area, a complex water-borne fishing culture has existed since prehistoric times and has added to the cultural mix.

Periodic breakdowns in the cultural system have occurred for a number of reasons. The demands for labor have, from time to time, led to population increases that push the limits of the ecological [[Wikipedia:carrying capacity|carrying capacity]], and, should a period of climatic instability ensue, a collapse of central government and declining populations can occur. Alternatively, military vulnerability to invasion from marginal hill tribes or nomadic pastoralists in the north has led to periods of trade collapse and neglect of irrigation systems.<ref>Thompson, Sukosh R. (2004) "Complexity, Diminishing Marginal Returns, and Serial Alzurian Fragmentation", (Vol 3, Journal of World-Systems Research).</ref> These trends have continued to the present day in [[Ukhdari]], and lesser so in [[Ealdorri]] too.
